chrome-syndicate-dreams.description:
Some connections were never meant to survive.

Following Afterimage, Chrome Syndicate Dreams marks the second collision between Grafenberg and Broken Shaman, and this time the connection has mutated.

Eleven tracks built for the space between the nightclub and the nervous system: relentless electronic pulses, colossal analog bass, motorik sequences, distorted synths, psychedelic flashes, vocoders, nocturnal melodies and hooks engineered to remain long after the system shuts down.

Grafenberg constructs the machine with surgical precision. Broken Shaman contaminates it.

His unstable, raw and unpredictable vocal presence cuts through immaculate electronic architecture, turning perfect sequences into something physical, damaged and unmistakably human. Throughout the record, mechanical repetition collides with desire, memory, obsession and loss.

From the immediate club ignition of Switch//ON and the artificial awakening of Boot Sequence, through Chrome Pulse, Black Market Heartware, Data Seduction and Firewall Kiss, the album moves deeper into a city where intimacy has become transmission and every connection leaves data behind.

By the time Neural Overdrive gives way to the hypnotic aftermath of System Collapse Ritual and the final signal of Last Transmission, the chrome surface has begun to fracture.

What started as a machine built to dance becomes something capable of remembering.

Or believing that it remembers.

Chrome Syndicate Dreams is infectious, obsessive, sensual and relentlessly kinetic: dark electro-pop, French electro pressure, psychedelic electronics and nocturnal club music fused into one continuous transmission.

Grafenberg x Broken Shaman.
Second contact.
Different system.
Higher voltage.

the-eastern-skylight-tapes.description:
THE EASTERN SKYLIGHT TAPES marks a new chapter in Grafenberg’s exploration of Anatolian electro, where Eastern scales, psychedelic guitars and ritual melodies collide with the precision of French Touch production.

Spiced, sensual and relentlessly rhythmic, the album moves between cosmic disco, techno, house, electro-rock and Anatolian psychedelia without ever losing its irresistible pop instinct. Huge basslines coil beneath glowing synthesizers, guitars burn through the mix, percussion spirals into trance, and every hook feels engineered to remain in the bloodstream.

This is a journey through a seductive parallel world where sugar becomes machinery, desire becomes code and romance bends across timelines. From the refracted emotion of Digital Love Refracted to the hypnotic propulsion of Eastern Sugar Machine, the cinematic ascent of Glitter in the Parallel Sky and the final confession of She Wrote the Code of Love, each track opens another passage beneath the eastern skylight.

Both futuristic and ancestral, elegant and feverish, THE EASTERN SKYLIGHT TAPES transforms the dancefloor into a psychedelic mirage. A powerful oriental wave built for bodies, hearts and minds in motion.

Written, produced and shaped by Grafenberg.
Released by Kinetic Distro.
tracklist: She wrote the code of love

parallel-sin-theory.description:
GRAFENBERG - PARALLEL SIN THEORY
Released by Kinetic Distro

Some stories don't end.

They fracture.

Parallel Sin Theory exists in the same haunted universe as The Wounds of Tomorrow, but through a broken mirror. If the previous album was about the wounds we carry, this one explores the infinite versions of ourselves born from those wounds.

Every regret becomes another timeline.
Every lost love creates another world.
Every impossible choice keeps living somewhere else.

At the center of this labyrinth stands Nyla Vey, delivering what may be her most mesmerizing performance yet. Ethereal and untouchable one moment, fierce and almost mechanical the next, she becomes the voice of countless parallel lives colliding into one hypnotic experience.

Musically, Grafenberg dives even deeper into his obsession with movement and emotion. French Touch grooves collide with robotic disco, haunted house music and futuristic electronic pop. Filtered disco loops, pounding 909 kick drums, distorted Moog basslines, vocoder choirs, ghostly harmonies and shimmering Anatolian motifs merge into a supernatural machine built for the dancefloor.

This is dystopian dance music.

An album where broken hearts become algorithms, angels are trapped beneath glass, forgotten futures refuse to die and every mirror hides another version of you waiting to take control.

From the explosive Daughter of the Parallel Flame to the heartbreaking Ashes of the Unchosen Path, from the sacred pulse of Vow of the Splintered Heart to the monumental title track, every song adds another reflection to an endless hall of fractured identities.

The journey culminates with Variant Godmode, an exclusive bonus track where all realities collapse into one final euphoric and apocalyptic celebration.

Mechanical.
Romantic.
Spooky.
Funky.
Irresistibly alive.

The Wounds of Tomorrow asked what survives after the fracture.

Parallel Sin Theory answers:

Everything does.
Just not in the same world.

the-wounds-of-tomorrow.description:
A shattered future never sounded this addictive.

With The Wounds of Tomorrow, Grafenberg delivers his most immediate, cinematic and dangerously catchy record to date. Built for decadent dancefloors and sleepless neon cathedrals, the album merges cosmic disco, pulse-driven electronic pop and dark orchestral grandeur into a hypnotic experience that feels both elegant and emotionally unstable.

At the center of the storm stands Nyla Vey, whose magnetic presence gives the album its bleeding heart. Her voice glides through fractured melodies, whispered confessions and explosive hooks while Grafenberg surrounds her with razor-sharp synth architecture, analog warmth and towering electronic textures.

Every track feels alive, wounded and seductive.

From the opening collapse of Tomorrow Bleeds First to the final emotional detonation of We Bleed Into The Future, Grafenberg constantly shifts shape without ever losing momentum. Wicked disco rhythms collide with eastern-inspired motifs, haunted vocoders, broken-glass atmospheres, cathedral-sized strings and massive analog synthesizers driven by Moog circuitry and Dave Smith machines.

The result is an album that moves with brutal elegance:
sensual but anxious,
beautiful but damaged,
danceable yet deeply haunted.

The Wounds of Tomorrow is not retro-futurism.
It is the sound of tomorrow already cracking apart under the lights.

For fans of sophisticated electronic pop, cosmic disco, dark synth-driven journeys and emotionally charged late-night soundtracks, this is Grafenberg at full power:
bolder, sharper, larger and more addictive than ever.

ghost-frequencies-for-lost-machines.description:
Some albums play in the background.
Others open a door.

“Ghost Frequencies for Lost Machines” unfolds like a waking dream — a warm, glowing horizon where emotion, memory and circuitry drift together in perfect balance.

A melted sun hangs low over an endless ocean.
Neon reflections shimmer.
Something soft, fragile and deeply human moves beneath the surface.

With this fifth album, Grafenberg pushes his signature sound into a more dreamy, hypnotic and intimate dimension. The textures are richer, the space wider, the emotions more suspended — like signals lost in time, still echoing somewhere in the night.

Across ten tracks, each piece feels like a fragment of a forgotten transmission:
haunting, sensual, and quietly alive.

✨ Silky falsetto vocals glide effortlessly
✨ Deep groovy basslines pulse beneath the skin
✨ Crisp, punchy drums keep everything grounded
✨ Shimmering synth layers and dreamy guitars blur the edges of reality
✨ Choruses bloom like distant memories you suddenly recognize

The sound blends modern psychedelic R&B pop, dream pop and subtle electronic elements into a lush, immersive experience — melancholic yet seductive, soft yet powerful.

Perfect for:

late-night drives under neon skies
slow dancing in silence
drifting between sleep and consciousness

Make love. Dance. Smile. Dream — awake or in your sleep.
Breathe in… and let it carry you. 

The signal is yours to keep on Bandcamp: https://kineticdistro.bandcamp.com/album/ghost-frequencies-for-lost-machines
tracklist: Soft reboot of a broken soul
The machine that dreamed of light

afterimage.description:
AFTERIMAGE is the first official collaboration between Grafenberg and Broken Shaman, a hypnotic collision where seductive futuristic hip-hop dissolves into precision-crafted electronic grooves.

Built on velvet-deep low end, cinematic synth architecture and late-night pulse mechanics, the track moves like the memory of a touch you can still feel long after the lights are gone. Grafenberg brings the cold elegance of elite electronic production, while Broken Shaman injects raw human tension, nocturnal magnetism and emotionally charged vocal presence.

The result is both intimate and massive: a high-end fusion of futuristic R&B textures, underground electronic sophistication, and urban after-hours storytelling.

AFTERIMAGE doesn’t just play.
It lingers.
Like neon on skin.
Like emotion trapped in glass.
Like the final image burned into your mind after the moment has already disappeared.

A first encounter.
A permanent trace.

the-halo-corruption-protocol.description:
Originally transmitted in March 2026, The Halo Corruption Protocol returns in its definitive form.

Rebuilt from the original production stems and completely remastered in 24-bit, this Enhanced Edition restores the depth, impact and internal detail of Grafenberg’s fourth album. Every voice, composition and lyric remains intact, but the entire sonic architecture has been rebuilt to reveal the album as it was always meant to exist.

Across ten interconnected tracks, sacred language is absorbed by machines and returned as corrupted code. Halos become surveillance devices, firmware becomes liturgy, damaged systems seek divinity, and technological collapse turns into a form of revelation.

From the cold activation of “Protocol Init. // Zero Sanctity” to the terminal ceremony of “Exit Ritual // Shutdown Liturgy”, the album unfolds as a complete cybernetic ritual: initiation, conversion, sanctification, corruption, system failure and final shutdown.

Dark synthesizers, industrial electronics, ritual vocals, distorted guitar textures, cinematic atmospheres and luminous 1980s melodic signals collide inside a machine-cathedral that can no longer distinguish grace from corruption.

This is not a rewrite of the album.

This is its definitive transmission.

CREDITS

Written, composed, produced and arranged by Grafenberg

Mixed and remastered in 24-bit by Grafenberg from the original stems

erebions-dominion.description:
Erebion’s Dominion is a full conceptual album.

Humanity doesn’t collapse because of a single enemy.
It collapses because it was already broken from the inside.

Then comes the signal.
Then comes the virus.

Not born from Earth — but sent from another world.
Not created to punish… but to reset.

The terrifying truth is simple:
the virus is not the villain of this story.
It is the cure.

Listen in order. No shuffle. Headphones recommended.
No hand remains to wield the sword.

the-error-gospel.description:
“The Error Gospel” is the nocturnal continuation of Grafenberg’s first album No Saints, No Proof — a descent into spiritual noise and analog devotion.
Ten tracks of dark electronic gospel, weaving Anatolian echoes, post-industrial pulses, and haunted sermons for the sleepless.

All tracks written and produced by Grafenberg.
Mastered in 2025.
Cover artwork by Grafenberg.

Listen loud — in the dark.

no-saints-no-proof.description:
Grafenberg’s debut full-length No Saints, No Proof is a hallucinatory collision of Anatolian psychedelia, dark electronic ritual, and surf-noir energy.
Ten tracks unravel like a midnight drive through shifting mirages: fuzz-saturated strings, trembling synths, hypnotic motorik drums, and a deep female voice bending between whispers and fire.

It is an album about memory and resistance — how glitches, ghosts, and fractured signals can become sacred. Ritual mantras (“Order Eats the Sun”, “Loom of Wires”) sit alongside spectral ballads (“Tape Ghost Mirage”, “VHS Desert Prayer”) and driving nocturnal anthems (“Motor Moon Communion”).

The sound is tactile, imperfect, and alive: warm compression, tape-delay halos, lo-fi grain.
For listeners of Gaye Su Akyol, Altın Gün, Tame Impala, and anyone seeking a darker, cinematic edge to psychedelic electronic music.

teopolis-recoded-ep.description:
Kinetic Distro – 2026

Some projects never truly disappear.
They wait.

Back in May 2015, Grafenberg released Teopolis, a debut EP on the now vanished German label Traumwelten Records. Created inside Ableton during long nights of experimentation, those tracks captured a moment in time: raw progressive energy, emotional synth work, hypnotic grooves and the feeling that electronic music could still open portals.

Eleven years later, those signals return.

TEOPOLIS RECODED is more than a remix EP.
It is a dialogue across time.

The original 2015 mixes have been rediscovered and restored alongside brand new reinterpretations crafted by Grafenberg himself and the dark electronic entity Chromabone. What once lived in a different era of underground progressive house has now evolved into something larger, deeper and strangely emotional.

Powered by modern production tools and the surreal possibilities of AI-assisted creativity, these tracks reconnect past and future:
gritty syncopated basslines, atmospheric synth architecture, gated vocal fragments, supersaw breakdowns and cinematic tension rebuilt for modern sound systems.

But beneath the technology lies something profoundly human:
the feeling of hearing your younger self again… and answering back through music.

This is not nostalgia.
This is resurrection.

Released by Kinetic Distro.

no-saints-no-proof-revisited.description:
While Grafenberg once reigned over a dystopian Anatolian-electro landscape,
Chromabone takes control of the trajectory.

No Saints, No Proof revisited is not a continuation, it is a shift of gravity.

Where the original work explored a vast, cinematic and myth-infused world, Chromabone strips it down to its core and redirects its energy toward the club. The result is a hypnotic, driving techno experience, built for motion, repetition, and total immersion.

Melodies become pulses.
Narratives become cycles.
Emotion becomes rhythm.

Each track is reconstructed from its skeletal form reduced, reshaped and re-engineered for the dancefloor. What remains is pure intention: a sound that doesn’t tell a story, but locks the body into it.

Chromabone doesn’t expand the universe.
He compresses it, into pressure, into tempo, into movement.

Released under Kinetic Distro, this project marks the emergence of a new force within the label: a presence designed for the club, for the night, for the moment where thought fades and only rhythm remains.

No saints. No proof. Only the loop.

visions.description:
Step into a fractured sonic dimension where memory, myth, and machine collide.

Visions is not just a remix playlist — it’s a reinterpretation of cultural echoes, a deep dive into the DNA of iconic artists reshaped through the unmistakable lens of Grafenberg. From the haunting atmospheres of Ghost to the emotional architecture of Tears for Fears, from the raw spirit of Nirvana to the dark gravity of Soundgarden, and the timeless melancholy of A-ha — each piece is rebuilt, not remixed.

These are deconstructed realities:
– Familiar melodies dissolve into cinematic textures
– Rhythms are re-engineered into hypnotic pulses
– Emotions are amplified, stretched, and reborn

Grafenberg doesn’t revisit — he reimagines.

Driven by a fusion of electronic noir, industrial elegance, and atmospheric storytelling, Visions transforms legendary tracks into something both nostalgic and entirely new — like hearing ghosts through neon light.

This playlist is a journey through:
Revisited classics. Reconstructed emotions. Reprogrammed memories.

Welcome to Visions.
Where the past doesn’t repeat — it mutates.

chaos-i-bleed-ep.description:
Chaos I Bleed distills Grafenberg’s dark union of Anatolian psychedelic rock and surf-noir into two definitive versions. The Original Ritual Cut rides a hypnotic pulse—saturated bağlama tracing kilim-like figures, tremolo guitars shimmering in vintage reverb, analog synths flickering like incense smoke. The Anatolian Night Drive Remix pushes the horizon wider: bass forward, motorik undertow, tape-delay halos and phased motifs built for late-night motion. Across both takes, the vocal moves from whisper to flame, carrying a subversive tension between order and rupture, intimacy and insurgency.

FFO: Altın Gün, Khruangbin (dark mode), The Limiñanas, Depeche Mode atmospheres, surf-psych cinema.
Best with: headphones / low lights / open road.
